topic: Sentence Connectors (Verbal Ability and Reading Comprehension)

sections.title: Basic Concept of Sentence Connectors
sections.content: Sentence connectors are words that link two sentences and clarify the relationship between them. Examples include and, but, because, so, therefore, and although. By using these connectors, two short sentences can be combined into one meaningful sentence.

sections.title: Types of Basic Connectors
sections.content: Some common connectors and their uses: And is used to add similar information. But is used to show opposition or contrast. Because is used to explain a reason. So or therefore is used to show a result. Although is used to show a contrasting situation.

sections.title: How to Choose the Correct Connector
sections.content: Step 1: Understand the meaning of both sentences. Step 2: Check whether the second sentence shows a reason, result, or contrast. Step 3: Choose the appropriate connector and combine the sentences accordingly. Example: I was tired. I went to sleep. → I was tired so I went to sleep.

sections.title: Common Meaning Relationships
sections.content: Addition: Joining two similar ideas (and). Contrast: Showing opposite ideas (but, although). Reason: Explaining a cause (because). Result: Showing an outcome (so, therefore).

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content: 1. Reversing the cause and result relationship. 2. Using 'and' when the sentences actually show contrast. 3. Using 'although' and 'but' together in the same sentence.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: Sentence connectors show the relationship between two sentences. To choose the correct connector, it is important to first understand the meaning and the logical relationship between the sentences.

tricks.title: Cause Connector Trick
tricks.explanation: If the second sentence explains the reason, use 'because'.
tricks.example: I stayed home because it was raining.

tricks.title: Result Connector Trick
tricks.explanation: If the second sentence shows a result, use 'so' or 'therefore'.
tricks.example: He studied hard so he passed the exam.

tricks.title: Contrast Connector Trick
tricks.explanation: If the sentences show opposite ideas, use 'but' or 'although'.
tricks.example: She was tired but she finished her work.

tricks.title: Addition Connector Trick
tricks.explanation: If both sentences give similar or additional information, use 'and'.

tricks.title: Meaning Check Trick
tricks.explanation: After adding the connector, the sentence should sound natural and logical.
tricks.example: It was late so we went home.

tricks.title: Connector Elimination Trick
tricks.explanation: Eliminate connectors that do not match the meaning of the sentence first.
tricks.example: Rain started so the match stopped.
